slides.headline: Rome Militarized Tipasa. Empires Left Ruins.
slides.subheadline: A trading post became an imperial foothold. Its ruins became the attraction.
slides.svgBlueprint: 600×750 viewBox; 40px safe margins. Dark paper field, orange kicker badge, white 64px condensed headline across four deliberate lines. Below, one monumental fractured-column silhouette: white upper shaft, orange fracture, dark surface plinth. Set subheadline at 22px. Bottom rule anchors two compact date badges and publication telemetry. No diagrams, arrows, or callout boxes.

slides.headline: Rome Turned Commerce Into Conquest
slides.subheadline: Claudius converted the Punic trading-post into a military colony targeting Mauretania’s kingdoms.

items.title: Imperial foothold
items.body: The trading-post became a military colony; later, a substantial Roman municipality.

items.title: Religious centre
items.body: The military foothold also became an important Christian hub under late Roman governorship.

slides.svgBlueprint: 600×750 viewBox; 40px margins. Use #0D0E12 background, #F1F3F9 text, #FF4D00 emphasis, #161820 cards. Stack two offset, full-width cards beneath a 44px headline. A faint harbour curve becomes a rigid orange military boundary behind the upper card. Lower card carries a restrained basilica silhouette. Integrate each badge into its card; no separate metric strip. Numerals 48px, bodies 22px. Illustrations are conceptual, not archaeological plans.

slides.kicker: THE HIDDEN DYNAMIC / IMPORTANCE IS NOT IMMUNITY
slides.headline: A Major City Was Still Vulnerable
slides.subheadline: Population and religious importance could not guarantee survival when imperial power changed hands.

items.title: The scale
items.body: Stéphane Gsell’s fourth-century population figure captures the city’s scale—not its security.

items.title: The rupture
items.body: Vandal destruction exposed the limits of a city’s accumulated Roman importance.

slides.svgBlueprint: 600×750 viewBox; 40px margins. #0D0E12 field with a full-width #161820 population placard. Render 20,000 at 84px in #F1F3F9, inhabitants separately at 24px. Place attribution directly below at 20px. An orange fracture interrupts the placard’s lower border, leading into one compact 430 CE consequence card. Headline 44px; card body 22px. Exactly two content groups; no decorative chart axes.

slides.headline: Reconstruction Could Not Defeat Demolition
slides.subheadline: Successive powers destroyed, rebuilt, and demolished the city; recovery never secured permanence.

items.title: Vandal destruction
items.body: The Vandals destroyed Tipasa, breaking the Roman city’s trajectory.

items.title: Byzantine reconstruction
items.body: The Byzantines reconstructed Tipasa, reversing destruction without guaranteeing survival.

items.title: Umayyad demolition
items.badge: the end of the seventh century
items.body: Umayyad forces demolished the city and reduced it to ruins.

slides.svgBlueprint: 600×750 viewBox; 40px margins. Three stacked milestones on a left-aligned spine. Use #FF4D00 broken segments for destruction and demolition; a #F1F3F9 repaired segment for reconstruction. Background #0D0E12; milestone panels #161820. Each panel contains its date, short title, and body only. Dates 26px, bodies 21px; wrap the final date across two lines. Preserve relative dates verbatim rather than inventing precise years. Timeline spacing is schematic, not proportional.

slides.headline: The Ruins Outlived Their Imperial Purpose
slides.subheadline: Modern Tipaza followed resettlement—not uninterrupted survival—and draws visitors to ancient ruins.

items.title: A new beginning
items.body: Nineteenth century resettlement preceded the modern town’s founding, after ancient Tipasa had become ruins.

items.title: A different attraction
items.body: Tourism rests mainly on the ancient ruins, alongside the sandy littoral.

slides.closingQuestion: What survives an empire: its intended power, or meanings it never controlled?
slides.svgBlueprint: 600×750 viewBox; 40px margins. Beneath a 44px headline, divide the body into two tall panels separated by an orange discontinuity. Left: #161820 with a fragmented foundation silhouette and 1857. Right: #0D0E12 with a quiet shoreline arc and the qualified population badge. Text #F1F3F9; accents #FF4D00. Metric numerals capped at 48px; keep nearly visibly attached to 30,000 and inhabitants below. Bodies 21px. Bottom full-width rule holds the closing question and tipaza.pub.
